alt: Paper 1 Section B is narrative or descriptive writing from a choice of scenario, prompt or image; Paper 2 Section B is a non-fiction viewpoint text with audience, purpose and form specified. On each paper, Section B gives 24 marks to content and organisation (AO5) and 16 to technical accuracy (AO6).
caption: Both papers end with a 40-mark writing task: 24 for AO5, 16 for AO6.

alt: A table of six purposes and their typical choices: describe (sensory detail, precise nouns and verbs), narrate (sequence, viewpoint character, pace), explain (logical order, causal connectives), instruct (imperatives, ordered steps), give and respond to information (accurate facts, measured register) and argue (position, evidence, counter-argument and rebuttal).
caption: Each purpose pulls the writing towards different choices.

alt: A large box labelled “controlling purpose: argue” holds an article arguing for a later school day. Inside it, explaining research, describing a tired morning and narrating a short anecdote each feed the argument.
caption: A text can mix purposes, but one purpose stays in control.

alt: A formality scale with two openings. To a head teacher, a formal letter: “I am writing to ask you to reconsider the decision to close the library at lunchtime.” To fellow students, an informal speech: “Raise your hand if the library has ever saved your lunchtime. Exactly.” Register also moves with sentence length, contractions, pronouns and humour.
caption: Match the register to the reader named in the task.

alt: Coherence is whether the whole text makes sense as a logical sequence; cohesion is the set of devices that bind it: topic sentences, discourse markers such as “however”, clear pronoun reference, lexical chains such as storm, thunder, drenched, and deliberate repetition. A text can be cohesive but incoherent.
caption: Plan the logic (coherence), then signal it (cohesion).

alt: The draft paragraph on school uniform is six disconnected sentences: the anecdote about a cousin is cut, the comfort point is saved for its own paragraph. The revision runs topic sentence, development of cost, signposted counter-argument about bullying, rebuttal with “however”, and a final sentence that links back to the topic.
caption: Group the ideas, signal the relationships, end where the topic sentence began.
